appearance.organs.*.shape.tube.why: A prickly pear's or a cholla's flower has no floral tube: its tepals open straight from the top of the pericarpel, a globose to top-shaped joint of stem that grows into the fruit, a little longer than the flower's radius (Anderson, The Cactus Family pp. 25 to 27 and 486).

traits.corolla_shape.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) pp. 25 to 27, 96 to 98 and 486: the prickly pears' and chollas' flowers cupped to disk-shaped, with many perianth parts and no floral tube above the pericarpel; Anderson's photographs of Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa and Opuntia engelmannii show the same cups.

traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 1, 1919, pp. 8 and 24), as their tribe Opuntieae, today's subfamily Opuntioideae: the only cacti whose areoles bear glochids (Maihuenia aside), and joints without ribs, their areoles scattered over them (Grusonia aside).

rules.note: The flower seated on its pericarpel with no floral tube: Anderson, The Cactus Family pp. 25 to 27 and 486; how much longer than the flower's radius is the model's choice.
